extracted.intended_audience: AISTATS 2025 paper reviewers / program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers evaluating submitted papers to the AISTATS 2025 conference, including how to score soundness, significance, novelty, clarity, reproducibility, ethics, and how to write constructive reviews and participate in rebuttal/discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Report problematic papers to the Area Chair (e.g., unacceptable formatting issues, dual submissions, plagiarism, etc.); submit high-quality reviews; during the rebuttal period, discuss with the other reviewers and the AC to help arrive at a good decision; recommend papers for oral talks, awards, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FAQ for list of problematic issues. Reviewer duties span detecting problems, producing constructive reviews, participating in author-reviewer discussion and AC discussion, and making recommendations for presentation/awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This part is invaluable to ACs and program chairs and helps authors determine misunderstandings needing response. Examples of contributions include theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, bridging fields, or critical analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 3 keywords about the paper’s topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Area Chairs to evaluate match between reviewer expertise and submission topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 3 keywords about your research expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether the reviewer’s expertise matches the submission’s research topic; discrepancies may indicate expertise mismatch and suggest using a lower confidence score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness (selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the soundness of the paper by selecting one: Correct; Minor errors (e.g., typo or errors that do not affect the main results); Major errors or trivial results (e.g., an incorrect theorem, or known results); Not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions mainly evaluate theoretical soundness if applicable. Incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection. Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite; avoid vague subjective complaints. Provide references if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for your provided judgment of soundness. If not applicable, put 'N/A'. If choice is 'minor errors' or 'major errors', specify details of concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thoroughly motivated criticism so authors can understand and potentially respond. Example comments provided (e.g., detailed note about a theorem error and its implication for results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the significance of the paper by selecting one: Significant with well supported statistical metrics and appropriate baselines; Somewhat significant (e.g., significant performance in some but not all experiments, missing a baseline); Not significant (e.g., overall similar to baselines, missing many baselines); Not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions mainly evaluate empirical significance. Comments should be detailed and specify missing baselines or experimental weaknesses. Example: note omitted baseline that’s appropriate because it differs only in one aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of your provided judgment of significance. If not applicable, put 'N/A'. If choice is 'somewhat significant' or 'not significant', specify details of concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why significance is reduced (e.g., missing baselines, partial improvements) and provide relevant citations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please assess the novelty of the paper by selecting one: Ground‑breaking new results; New results; Incremental compared to existing results; Known results, or trivial extension of known results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty relative to existing literature and cite relevant prior works. Prefer solid technical exploration or new directions over small incremental advances. Do not use generic criteria (e.g., 'research area is important' or 'well-written').

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of your provided judgment of novelty. If your choice is 'incremental' or 'known results' please specify previous publication(s) that support your choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations and concrete explanations of how the submission relates to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-conventional contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission contain non-conventional research contributions? Examples: novel ideas with not widely accepted assumptions, new problems/tasks, 'bridging fields' contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on non-conventional aspects, especially assumptions, model designs and methods that are not yet widely accepted. Recognize value of out‑of‑the‑box ideas and avoid dismissive criticism due to unfamiliarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written? Is it well organized?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the paper has clearly stated contributions, notation and results; explained theoretical assumptions; motivated methodology with examples. A superbly written paper provides enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results. If unclear, make constructive suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which related works are discussed: All related works are clearly discussed; All related works cited but discussion less clear; Some minor related works missing or described incorrectly; Some important related works missing or described incorrectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in Additional Comments whether the submission suitably relates to prior work — not just listing but explaining differences. Note that works appearing less than 4 months before submission are considered concurrent and detailed comparisons are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add additional comments, feedback and suggestions for improvement, and further questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague, subjective complaints. Be constructive and help authors understand your viewpoint. Suggest what you would do differently to improve the paper. Remember you are reviewing scientific contribution, not your interest level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there enough details to reproduce the main experimental results? Options: Sufficient amount of details available for reproducing the main results; Some amount of details available; Insufficient amount of details available; Not applicable (no experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether assumptions, experimental settings and limitations are clearly stated in paper and supplementary material. If not, list this as a weakness in Additional Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall rating on 1–5 scale: 5 Top 10% of accepted papers; 4 Accept; 3 Borderline accept; 2 Borderline reject; 1 Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating should reflect your assessment of the submission’s contributions. Do NOT assume assigned sample is representative or adjust scores to match conference acceptance rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence in your assessment, 1–5: 5 Absolutely certain; 4 Confident; 3 Fairly confident; 2 Somewhat confident; 1 Educated guess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly for 5. Compare your Paper Keywords and Expertise Keywords to gauge whether you are familiar enough to be certain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns (selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns? Options: No concern; Minor concerns; Major concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether paper discusses potential negative societal impact and/or ethical issues. If not, assess if the paper should include this point. This ethics assessment is independent of overall rating; flag for additional ethical review if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concern justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of your provided judgment of ethical concerns. If not applicable, put 'N/A'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the nature of the ethical concern (bias, harm, application misuse, dataset issues, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to abide by the AISTATS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to the AISTATS Code of Conduct; reviewers must adhere to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep the paper and supplementary materials (including code submissions and LaTeX source), as well as the reviews, confidential. This includes deleting any submitted code at the end of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share or retain submission materials beyond the review process; comply with confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comment to Area Chair (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field for confidential comments to the Area Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for explicit comparisons to other submissions, minor formatting issues, or more blunt criticisms. If you inadvertently discover author identities, do not divulge them. These comments are not shown to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be thoughtful
rubrics_metrics.description: Be thoughtful. The paper may have been written by a first-year graduate student; don't crush their spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive and considerate in tone; avoid unnecessarily harsh language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be fair
rubrics_metrics.description: Be fair. Do not let personal feelings affect your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on scientific content and avoid bias based on authors, institutions, or topic familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Be useful. A good review is useful to authors, other reviewers, and area chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable suggestions and clear reasoning so all stakeholders can benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific. Do not make vague statements in your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific criticisms are fairer and easier for authors to address than vague complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Be flexible. Authors may address points in the discussion; update your understanding and revise reviews accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an effort to read author responses and update your review to reflect new information rather than ignoring rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: be timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Be timely. Respect deadlines and respond promptly during discussion. If you cannot complete your review on time, inform the Area Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews enable proper discussion and decisions. If pressured to provide a biased review, notify Program Chairs. Report unethical or suspect behavior to Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and (if appropriate) respond to each author’s response before decisions are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore any author response. Update your review to indicate you read the response and whether you agree or disagree; be specific about why your opinion remains or changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of LLMs is not allowed to write papers, reviews, and meta-reviews. They can be used as an assist tool (e.g., to check grammar). Reviewers/authors are ultimately responsible for text they write, including LLM-generated content that could be plagiarism or fabrication. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are responsible for any content generated with LLM assistance; avoid using LLMs to generate substantive scholarly text that could violate policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling links in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may contain links (e.g., URLs) to external materials such as code. Reviewers are recommended not to follow such links; treat them as authors' statements that materials will be made available if accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you access a link, be aware it may reveal your involvement in reviewing and potentially de-anonymize you. The conference cannot guarantee safety of external links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling GitHub/code links
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing code is optional. If accessing anonymous GitHub links, download or clone after logging out of your own GitHub account; do not fork the repository as this might reveal your identity. Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take precautions to preserve anonymity and security when accessing submitted code. Reviewing code is optional and not required for the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is explicitly allowed and there is a separate submission deadline for it. Looking at supplementary material is optional for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible that appended supplementary material and separately uploaded supplement do not conflict. Update (Sept 20, 2024): if they conflict, reviewers are free to consider either version. Supplementary material remains optional for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor formatting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor formatting issues (e.g., different citation styles) should not lead to desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag formatting issues but do not change score/evaluation because of them; organizers will ensure correct style if paper is accepted.
